site.tagline: U.S. stock market history, visualised: a century of prices, valuation and drawdowns, refreshed every trading day.
site.description: History of Market is a data-visualisation site for the history of the U.S. stock market. More than a century of prices, valuations, drawdowns and index membership — the S&P 500 since 1928, the Dow since 1914, the Nasdaq since 1971, the semiconductor, technology, financial and consumer sectors, and the Magnificent 7 — drawn as charts, arranged by sector into volumes and chapters, and refreshed automatically after every U.S. trading-day close. Professional investors use it to place today's market inside a hundred-year frame: where the cycle stands, and which patterns recur. Its charts are cited by investors, researchers and media in more than 80 countries. Every chart names its source and can be shared or embedded; the data behind it is published as open JSON (CC BY 4.0, attribution required). Each volume is a handful of short chapters that each answer one question: the shape of returns, the anchors of valuation (Shiller CAPE, trailing and forward P/E, year-by-year valuation × EPS decomposition), the rhythm of crisis, the anatomy of the index.
